name: aws-lc-rs (AWS-LC with a ring-compatible API)
baseline: RustCrypto aes-gcm 0.11.1, p256 0.14.0, p384 0.14.0 and rsa 0.10.0-rc.19 on x86_64
verdict_reason: On the same independent benchmark (Ryzen 9 7940HS), aws-lc-rs encrypts AES-256-GCM at 9.48 GiB/s against 2.92 GiB/s for RustCrypto, signs RSA-2048 about 10.7x faster and ECDSA P-384 about 4.5x faster. It is first or second on every x86_64 row and well ahead of ring on P-384.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark by graviola's author with CPU and crate versions stated; rustc version and flags are not shown.
claimed_speedup: AES-256-GCM 8 KB: 9.48 GiB/s vs 2.92 GiB/s (3.2x, derived from page data); RSA-2048 signing: 5,487.4 vs 514.3 sigs/sec (10.7x, derived from page data); ECDSA P-384 signing: 16,583 vs 3,656.4 sigs/sec (4.5x, derived from page data); P-384 key agreement: 7,359.1 vs 795.15 kx/sec
workload: graviola's criterion suite: AES-256-GCM encryption of 8 KB buffers, RSA-2048 and ECDSA P-256/P-384 signing and verification, X25519/P-256/P-384 key agreement, ML-KEM-768.
hardware: Framework 16 laptop with AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS; MacBook Pro M2 (2022)
os: Linux on the x86_64 laptop; macOS on the M2
platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows and other targets AWS-LC supports; optional FIPS build
one_liner: Rust bindings to AWS-LC with ring's API: 3.2x RustCrypto's AES-GCM throughput and 10x its RSA-2048 signing rate on a Ryzen 9 7940HS.
how_it_is_fast: AWS-LC is a BoringSSL fork with hand-written assembly for AES-GCM, RSA and the NIST curves; aws-lc-rs calls it through pre-generated FFI bindings. It carries AVX-512 code paths (the benchmark page marks its x86_64 AES-GCM and RSA signing results as using AVX-512) and much faster P-384 code than ring, which is where it pulls ahead of ring.
use_it_when: rustls or other TLS stacks where handshake and AEAD cost matter
caveats: No run date or rustc version on the page (served Last-Modified 2026-10-27)
The page marks the x86_64 AES-GCM and RSA signing results as using AVX-512; CPUs without it will see smaller gaps
On the M2 run the RustCrypto AES-GCM figure (0.142 GiB/s vs 6.47 GiB/s) used aes-gcm 0.10.3, whose ARMv8 AES path needed opt-in flags, so that gap is overstated
tradeoffs: Needs a C/C++ compiler; FIPS builds also need CMake and Go
Large C dependency compiled into the binary

evidence.quote: rustcrypto version: aes-gcm 0.11.1, p256 0.14.0, p384 0.14.0, rsa 0.10.0-rc.19, sha2 0.11.1
Consuming projects will need a C/C++ compiler to build.
